work.text: In a forest pavilion, bamboo and trees give thickly overlapping shade, Seeking friends crying "ying," I too am fond of music.
work.lead: Ni Zan’s poem on the painting:

source.author: Ni Zan

work.text: I sketched [this] painting of "Poetic Thoughts in a Forest Pavilion," and wrote the poem in order to leave it behind for the multi-talented Youxin

source.author: Ni Zan
source.title: Inscription on Poetic Thoughts in a Forest Pavilion, translated by the Art Institute of Chicago

moment.text: After his death his pictures became so highly appreciated that the Kiang-nan families were divided into two classes; such that possessed, and such that did not possess pictures by Ni Tsan.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

matters.text: During his lifetime, his work was highly valued and in itself was enough to pay for the hospitality provided by his friends as he travelled.
I am no hireling artist, a hanger-on at rich men's doors.
